cases.title: Admit an explicit supported profile and reject ambiguous release identity
cases.risk: A default, unsupported value or exception decision authorizes the wrong routine release.

conditions: Use the valid routine profile with package version 0.3.5, tag v0.3.5, latest channel and codex/claude targets. Start every mutation from this valid baseline.

when: Resolve the tag-owned profile and load it directly and by tag.

Independently remove or corrupt the profile, remove a required field, mismatch the version, or introduce an unsupported closed value. Pair an unknown channel/target/kind with a version mismatch to observe rejection precedence.
Parse a special profile with an explicit exception decision and assess routine eligibility.
then: The valid input resolves to docs/releases/profiles/v0.3.5.yaml and retains its declared package, version, targets and required safeguards.
Missing/malformed input identifies its path or field; unknown values reject before consistency diagnostics. No defaults silently authorize a different release.
Special classification remains outside routine automation even with an owner decision.

gaps: Unknown kind, target and channel now start from accepted private profiles and compete with an explicit version mismatch. The remaining missing-field, malformed, version-mismatch and special-decision methods use standalone fixtures rather than establishing the same accepted private baseline before each mutation.

cases.title: Preparation ownership distinguishes generated, human and historical material
cases.risk: Live inventory consumption disappears while isolated parser fixtures still pass.

conditions: Use the selected surface inventory and valid fixture; mutate one ownership classification or override rationale at a time.

when: Load the selected inventory and resolve its declared surfaces; repeat with missing/unknown classification or an unexplained override.
then: Resolve the independently declared paths to generated, human-checked and immutable-history ownership.
Reject missing/unknown ownership and unexplained overrides rather than allowing a write.

cases.title: Literal ownership distinguishes existing drift from unauthorized changes
cases.risk: Drift is silently accepted or the live resource path is orphaned.

conditions: Use the actual selected baseline and a fresh literal fixture; distinguish current generated, historical and unauthorized literals.

when: Read the baseline, inspect unchanged drift, then introduce unknown classification, missing ownership or unexplained historical classification.
then: Existing classified drift is reported; generated values identify their owner and historical values retain their rationale.
Unknown or incomplete classification rejects with an attributable diagnostic; a historical version literal alone grants no release support.

cases.title: Resolve reviewed version intent without inventing a release decision
cases.risk: The numeric increment supplies invented engineering intent.

conditions: Use package 0.5.1, reviewed patch rationale and provider version 0.5.0. Run malformed intent and publication-state alternatives independently.

when: Resolve version intent and derive the routine profile.
Repeat with missing/unknown decision, inconsistent increment, already-published unchanged source and changed source without new version intent.
Validate the same intent in offline CI without provider eligibility observations.
then: The supported patch derives 0.5.1/latest and retains the reviewed rationale.
Missing or inconsistent intent stops; already-published unchanged work reports no-op, while changed source needs a new version decision.
Offline intent validity supplies no public eligibility or publication authority.
